title: Understanding Full Column Rank
text: A matrix is full column rank if its columns are linearly independent. This means no column can be written as a linear combination of the others.

title: Dummy Variables and Linear Independence
text: When using dummy variables for categorical data, each variable represents a category. If one category can be perfectly predicted by the others, the matrix is not full column rank.

title: Analyzing the Design Matrix
text: In the design matrix X, each column represents a food item. If a student eats all four foods, the sum of the columns for that row will be $$4$$. Can any column be expressed as a combination of the others?

hintAnswer: Yes, if one column can be expressed as a sum of others, the matrix is not full column rank.
title: Checking Linear Independence
text: Consider the columns of the design matrix X. Are there any columns that can be expressed as a linear combination of the others?
choices: Yes, if one column can be expressed as a sum of others, the matrix is not full column rank.
